correctness.rationale: On infinite compact Hausdorff K the derived set K_prime is nonempty closed compact. For each slice determined by a norm-one regular signed measure mu, choose a non-isolated point t attaining beta=max_{K_prime}|f| and a nearby point s with arbitrarily small atomic variation mass. Regularity gives a neighborhood W with small |mu|(W); Urysohn bump interpolation from any slice witness g0 to opposite sign at s changes the functional by < slice slack while creating distance at least 1+beta-epsilon. For upper bound isolated exceptional points F={isolated t:|f(t)|>beta+epsilon} are finite by compactness/cluster point continuity; a single slice based on the average of their signed point evaluations forces every g to have the correct sign on F, and outside F distance <=1+beta+epsilon. Hence equality for all f in the full unit ball. The c specialization follows because K_prime={infinity}. No special metrizability or measure atomlessness is assumed.
residual_risks: The precise assertion is real C(K) for K infinite compact Hausdorff, not complex uniform algebra or Delta constant.
